newsitem.title: USA: Shabazz grandson pleads guilty to fire.
newsitem.headline: Shabazz grandson pleads guilty to fire.

text.p: Twelve-year-old Malcolm Shabazz pleaded guilty on Thursday to charges of setting the fire that killed his grandmother Betty Shabazz, widow of slain black civil rights leader Malcolm X.
"I set a fire," the boy said without emotion in Family Court in Yonkers, New York, when asked what he did. The charges were the juvenile equivalent of second degree manslaughter and arson.
"That's all we need to know," Judge Howard Spitz replied, interrupting the proceedings.

A hearing was scheduled for next Tuesday and the boy was expected to be sentenced later this month. The maximum sentence he could get is 18 months, but he could be kept in a detention facility until he is 18 years old.
Betty Shabazz, 63, died on June 23 from burns she suffered over 80 percent of her body in the June 1 fire. The New York City medical examiner has ruled her death a homicide.
Her grandson was accused of setting the fire with gasoline while staying at her apartment in Yonkers, north of New York City.
He is the son of Qubilah Shabazz, one of six daughters Betty Shabazz had with Malcolm X, who was assassinated at the Audubon Ballroom in Manhattan on Feb. 21, 1965.
Qubilah Shabazz was seated in the courtroom and watched as her son spoke. The two did not exchange any words.
Shabazz family attorney Percy Sutton said he had instructed the boy to plead guilty in order to shorten the process.
Sutton said it was a "terrible day" for the boy and "a tragic day in the life of his family."
Sutton said young Malcolm was remorseful, loved his grandmother and was very sorry for what had happened.
